newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends higher as bullish tone dominates.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends higher as bullish tone dominates.

text.p: Wall Street stocks finished broadly higher on Wednesday, buoyed by fresh reports of strong corporate earnings growth and a widespread perception that the Federal Reserve does not intend to raise interest rates anytime soon.
The Dow industrials rose 27 points to 8088, its second consecutive all-time closing high. Several broader indices also rallied to records.
The gains came as Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan concluded his two-day report to Congress on the state of the U.S. economy.
During his testimony, Greenspan repeated his rosy, moderate growth/low inflation appraisal of the economy and reinforced analysts' impression that an imminent increase in interest rates was unlikely.
"I think the die was cast yesterday," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities. "In effect, Greenspan has told us not to worry about the August or September Fed meetings."
Stocks surged early on Greenspan's comments but faded a bit when Federal Reserve Vice Chairman Alice Rivlin later cautioned that it was a "close call" on whether rates should rise.
The comments tempered but failed to quash Wall Street's enthusiasm, given Greenspan's upbeat assessment of affairs.
"Alan Greenspan really rules the Fed," Wachtel said.
With their interest rate worries allayed, investors were again free to focus on corporate earnings, where the trend remained positive.

Among Dow components, chemical and energy company DuPont Co gained 1-7/16 to 67-5/8 after reporting second-quarter net income rose 14 percent versus a year ago. AlliedSignal Inc, which posted an earnings increase of 16 percent before special items, gained 1-1/16 to 92-1/4.
The results highlighted another day of strong earnings reports and buttressed the stock market in its relentless climb into record territory.

"There's no reason to buy stocks other than to participate in the earnings growth of the companies and the second-quarter results have generally been coming in above consensus," said Al Goldman, market analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons.
The Dow got its biggest lift from Boeing Co, which climbed 2-11/16 to 59-1/16 after winning European Union approval for its merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp.
Shares in McDonnell Douglas rose 4-5/16 to 76-1/16.
Computer Associates International Inc surged 5-1/4 to 69-9/16 after the software company reported fiscal first-quarter earnings jumped 30 percent, beating Wall Street estimates.

There were disappointments, however. Anheuser-Busch Cos Inc fell 2-5/8 to 45-1/4 after it reported slightly higher second-quarter earnings and said full-year earnings growth would fall slightly below long-term objectives because of heavy discounting in the beer industry.
The S&P 500 index rose 2.58 to 936.56.
The NYSE Composite rose 1.62 to 485.51, a record.
The Nasdaq Composite gained 3.79 points to 1567.65.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
